messages:
oncall-bot: ALERT: cb-serving-prod group experiencing sustained tail latency + request queue growth (>120s p99). Trigger: continuous-batcher throughput drop and kv_cache size spike. Page: oncall-sre.
oncall-bot: Details: affected models: text-gen-v2 variants, region: us-west-2, symptom: queue depth > 3k, inflight microbatches piling, KV cache eviction rate 50k/s.
samir.k: I’m on it — grabbing logs and metrics. Can someone attach the latest cb-scheduler logs?
lee: grabbing logs now, links coming. looks like microbatch sizes collapsed to 1 frequently, lots of small batches and severe scheduling jitter.
jess: @samir.k tagging you — consoles show KV_CACHE_BYTES at 1.9GB (normal ~400MB) and eviction churn. We saw this pattern during last runaway.
maria.ops: customer impact? any 5xxs / timeouts surfacing to customers?
support-bot: Customer alerts: 3 high-priority SLO alerts from enterprise customers (one on Dedicated). Some requests are timing out at app layer ~30s.
samir.k: hypothesis: under high concurrency CB is creating many tiny microbatches => kv cache growth due to many hot key entries and less efficient reuse, causing eviction storms and scheduler thrash.
lee: agree. also seeing continuous-batch controller backpressure loop — when batch waits for min_microbatch it times out then flushes, creating flood of tiny batches.
jess: mitigation options: 1) temporarily disable continuous batching for text-gen-v2; 2) bump min_microbatch_size to 4-8; 3) apply jitter to batch flush timer to smooth spikes. Which do we do first?
maria.ops: priority: restore customer latency ASAP. Option 1 is fastest — disable CB for the model in routing -> instant fall back to microbatching/no-cb code path. But cost increases.
samir.k: +1 for temporary disable on affected partition(s) while we stabilize. We should target us-west-2 AZ1 nodes first.
lee: prepping rollout. plan: 1) patch route config for model text-gen-v2: set continuous_batching.enabled=false for pool cb-prod-az1; 2) monitor queue depth for 5m; 3) if stable, roll to other AZs.
/devdeploy-bot: executing change: PATCH /route-configs/text-gen-v2/pools/cb-prod-az1 {"continuous_batching": {"enabled": false}} — in progress.
/devdeploy-bot: rollout complete (2/2 controllers).
jess: seeing immediate drop in microbatch churn. queue depth down ~70% in first 40s. KV cache eviction rate falling.
support-bot: customer alerts: reduced error rate for affected customers — follow-up messages to customers queued.
maria.ops: can we also run a quick hotfix to the batch controller to add jitter and raise min_microbatch_size before re-enabling? Less risk to revert.
samir.k: Yes. I'll prepare config patch: set min_microbatch_size=4, add flush_jitter_ms=15, cap max_microbatch_wait_ms=120. Applying to canary nodes first.
lee: logs show a set of heavy prefix variety causing many distinct KV keys per request. Lowering parallelism + higher min_microbatch should increase reuse and reduce unique cache entries.
/devdeploy-bot: deploying cb-controller-config v2026.3.15-hotfix to pool cb-prod-az1-canary.
/devdeploy-bot: canary deployed (3 nodes).
jess: monitoring canary for 3 minutes — p99 latency and queue depth trending down. KV cache size dropping toward baseline.
maria.ops: what about throttles? Do we need a temporary ingress rate-limit for some noisy tenants as a protective measure?
samir.k: good idea. I propose a per-tenant soft-rate limit for top-3 requesters with large prefix variance while we validate. Support can identify candidates.
support-bot: Identified tenants: corp-alpha, analytics-pro, sandbox-team. I'll file soft-rate-limit tickets and add them to the change.
lee: can we re-enable continuous batching on canary with the new config to validate behavior under load?
samir.k: re-enable on canary now.
/devdeploy-bot: PATCH /route-configs/text-gen-v2/pools/cb-prod-az1-canary {"continuous_batching": {"enabled": true}} — in progress.
/devdeploy-bot: re-enable complete on canary.
jess: canary metrics look good: microbatch size median=6, jitter smoothing visible, KV cache churn down 10x, p99 latency reduced to baseline + ~5%.
maria.ops: if canary holds for 10m we can stage roll to remaining nodes. recommend leaving soft-rate-limits active for 30m.
support-bot: customers notified: sent status update and told them we’re rolling and monitoring. No new escalations.
samir.k: rolling to AZ1 remaining nodes now with same config. staging ~50% of nodes, watching.
/devdeploy-bot: rolling config to cb-prod-az1 nodes (batch size 10).
jess: roll progressing. watchlist: queue depth, kv_eviction_rate, microbatch_size distribution. current: queue depth steady, eviction rate trending down.
lee: roll complete for AZ1. proposing to proceed to AZ2 if stable for 5m.
maria.ops: go for AZ2. notify SRE oncall for CS handoff in 30m.
support-bot: All affected customer alerts cleared. No active incidents open.
oncall-bot: NOTE: Incident under mitigation; oncall handoff scheduled to samir.k -> lee at 2812347055 (15m).
samir.k: leaving notes in runbook: root cause suspected interaction between continuous batching controller backpressure and high concurrency request patterns creating microbatch collapse and KV cache cardinality spike. Hotfix: raised min_microbatch_size, added flush jitter, and temporarily applied per-tenant soft rate limits.
jess: postmortem action items: 1) add automatic detection for microbatch collapse patterns (lots of size=1 flushes), 2) add circuit-breaker that auto-disables CB per-pool when KV cache eviction rate spikes > X, 3) stress test CB under high concurrency with synthetic prefix-variance loads.
maria.ops: opening postmortem ticket and scheduling incident review tomorrow 10:00am PT. tagging infra, ml, and support.
support-bot: customer follow-up: sent summary and ETA for detailed postmortem.
lee: thanks team. I'll take oncall for next shift and continue monitoring. if anything flares, re-pager. :thumbsup: 
samir.k: thanks everyone — leaving logs and dashboard links in the thread.
oncall-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.
